subject: Throughput acceptance + on-prem test plan for private GPU pool
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@datanest.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@datanest.ai
Date: Sun, 14 Nov 2027 15:03:00 +0000
Subject: Throughput targets & acceptance criteria for private GPU pool

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for the quick intro call. To get the procurement cycle moving we need to lock down acceptance criteria for the on-prem/private deployment. High-level asks from our side: 

- Sustained throughput: 120 inference requests/sec (p95 latency target 200ms) for our standard payloads (avg token length ~120).
- Burst tolerance: absorb spikes up to 350 req/sec for short windows (~3–5 minutes) without failing requests.
- Network constraint: our DC uplink to the compute rack is 10Gbps with a 1.2ms fiber RTT to the application frontends.

We'd like Redwood to propose a concrete test plan (what you will provision, how you'll measure, and pass/fail criteria). Procurement is aligned on a 3-month pilot if acceptance is met.

Can you propose a minimal configuration and a runbook for the acceptance test? We can loop in our infra (cc'd procure contact for early procurement questions).

Thanks,
Oliver Grant
Head of ML Infrastructure 
DataNest
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@datanest.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 10:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Throughput targets & acceptance criteria for private GPU pool

Hi Oliver —

Really helpful summary. I've sketched an initial mutual action plan and a conservative minimal configuration for the acceptance window (attached: datanest_mutual_action_plan.xlsx). Key points up front: 

- Proposal (minimal): 6 x A100-equivalent GPUs in a private pool, dedicated NICs (25Gbps per node if possible), and a warm pool policy to keep KV caches hot.
- Autoscale baseline: scale floor 6 GPUs, scale ceiling 12 GPUs; target sustained servicing on the floor, burst to ceiling for short windows.
- Acceptance test: 90-minute soak at 120 req/s (p95 < 200ms), then three controlled burst ramps to 350 req/s for 3 minutes each. No more than 1% request failure across the entire run.
- Measurement: Redwood will provide per-token latency histogram, GPU util, NIC throughput, and request success/failure logs. We'll deliver a pass/fail report and raw metrics.

Open items for our infra team: what is the effective network path (oversubscription at top-of-rack), preferred NIC speeds, and any egress policies that could shape traffic? Vivek, can you advise on our recommended NIC/oversub ratios for a 10Gbps customer uplink?

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal sizing confirmation (Laura + Vivek) —> send concrete GPU/NIC counts and assumptions.
2) We send a runbook and test harness (JMeter + tokenized samples) and a Drive link with scripts.
3) Alignment call this week with DataNest infra to confirm test window and schedule.

Drive link and HubSpot deal attached below.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Throughput targets & acceptance criteria for private GPU pool

Kimberly / team —

Quick sizing math and assumptions so we have deterministic talk-track for the call with DataNest:

Assumptions:
- Benchmarking baseline: 1 A100-equivalent GPU can sustain ~22 req/s for the target payload at p95=200ms (this is conservative based on our internal tests with Redwood-optimized kernels, batching disabled for latency SLO).
- Network: each request carries ~17KB average egress (model output + small metadata). At 350 req/s sustained over 3 minutes that's ~35MB/s ~280Mbps — so the 10Gbps uplink is not the limiter for token egress; NIC saturation will show up when multiple tenants share the same top-of-rack uplink.

Sizing:
- Sustained 120 req/s -> 120 / 22 ≈ 5.5 -> round up to 6 GPUs (matches Kimberly's floor).
- Burst to 350 req/s -> 350 / 22 ≈ 16 GPUs. We should not expect to burst to 16 on a single private pool for cost reasons; instead propose staged burst with fast fallback to degraded latency target or spillover to a compatible model variant.

Recommendation:
- Minimal acceptance config: 6 GPUs (floor) with a short-term staged burst plan up to 12 GPUs (ceiling) inside the private pool; for acceptance testing we will provision temporary capacity on 12 GPUs and run controlled bursts to observe behavior.
- Warm pool: pre-warm KV caches on at least 60% of the floor nodes before the acceptance window.
- Network: request DataNest reserve dedicated NIC LAGs (2x25Gb or single 25Gb per node) where possible. If their rack is strictly 10Gbps, advise limiting simultaneous node fan-out to avoid top-of-rack oversubscription above 80%.

I've attached a short CSV with the calc table. Once Vivek confirms NIC guidance I'll convert this to the mutual action plan artifacts.

Laura Bennett
Lead Capacity Planner | Redwood Inference

Attachments: sizing_calc_20271116.csv
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Throughput targets & acceptance criteria for private GPU pool

Team —

Operational notes from an infra/ops perspective (callouts for the runbook):

- NIC sizing: if DataNest can only offer 10Gbps per top-of-rack, we must expect oversubscription when we do multi-node bursts. Recommend they carve a dedicated 10Gbps path for the private pool test or allow LACP across two 10Gbps uplinks to give us headroom during bursts.
- Warm pool: implement an automated warmup step that issues representative prefix requests for 15 minutes prior to the main soak. This reduces cold-KV miss amplification during the first ramp.
- Admission and graceful degradation: acceptance harness should include a policy test that verifies our fallback chain (scaled model variant + degraded latency target) so that we can show safe degradation instead of hard failures.
- Measurement hooks: we need SNMP or sFlow counters from DataNest's TOR switches during the ramp to correlate NIC drops with request failures. Add that as an item for their infra team to expose during the test window.

Ops runbook excerpt attached (ops_runbook_excerpt.txt). I can draft the full runbook tonight; we should share it with DataNest before the call.

Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
